output:
I ran the `--review-pr` checklist against every rule in `rules.json` (no project filter), limited to `git diff e88f1979…HEAD` (25 files). No tracked files were modified; the checklist was written to my scratchpad, not into `docs/`. I didn't run tests and didn't use the lookup zoom for any rule. I found one medium issue and four low ones.

## Findings

| # | Rule | Severity | Location | Finding |
|---|------|----------|----------|---------|
| 1 | TEST-07 / TEST-02 | Medium | `src/modules/relay/routes/relay.controller.integration.spec.ts:2944` (and the POST relay block) | **The new 403 path has no route-level test.** The PR changes how the relayer is chosen: it now comes from the chain's config-service `relayerType` instead of env config. It also adds `RelayerNotAvailableExceptionFilter` to both `POST /relay` and `GET /relay/:safeAddress`. But no integration test sends a chain with `relayerType: null` or `GTF` and checks the 403 body. The only tests of those errors are in `relay.manager.spec.ts`. That proves the switch statement, not that the filter is wired to the routes. Add one 403 smoke test per route. |
| 2 | CONFIG-05 / PR-02 | Low | `.env.sample.json:1161`, `.env.sample.json:1167` | **Removed env vars are still documented.** `RELAY_DAILY_LIMIT_CHAIN_IDS` is still marked `"required": true`, and `RELAY_FEE_CHAIN_IDS` is still listed. The PR deleted both from `configuration.schema.ts` and `configuration.ts`, so the env metadata no longer matches the runtime. Remove both entries. |
| 3 | NAME-01 | Low | `src/modules/relay/domain/relay.manager.ts:7`, `:39` | **Unneeded import alias.** `type RelayerType as RelayerTypeValue` isn't needed, because `RelayerType` is already both the const value and the type. `relay-manager.interface.ts` in the same diff uses `RelayerType \| null` directly. Drop the alias so the two files match. |
| 4 | TYPE-06 | Low | `src/modules/chains/domain/entities/__tests__/chain.builder.ts:57` | **Cast that isn't needed.** Without the cast, `faker.helpers.arrayElement([...Object.values(RelayerType), null])` already has the type `RelayerType \| null`, so `as Chain['relayerType']` adds nothing. If a type drifts later, the cast will hide it instead of letting the compiler catch it. Remove it. |
| 5 | PR-02 / TYPE-04 | Low | `src/modules/relay/routes/relay.controller.ts:78`, `:155` | **The new 403 isn't in Swagger.** Both endpoints can now return 403 (no relayer defined, or relayer type not implemented). Neither has an `@ApiForbiddenResponse`. For `GET :safeAddress` this is a new status code. |

## Worth a look (not a rule failure)

- **CHANGE-04 / LOG-01, backward compatibility:** before this PR, a chain with no relayer config fell back to `DailyLimitRelayer`; the removed comment said it was "for backward compatibility". Now it gets a 403 from `relay.manager.ts:59`.
  - `chain.schema.ts:108` uses `.catch(null)`, so a missing field or an unknown relayer type from the config service also ends up as that 403, and nothing is logged.
  - Relaying on any chain stops working until the config service sets `relayerType` for it. Make sure that's in place before deploying.
  - A `warn` log when the value fails to parse would make this easier to spot. The `.catch` itself follows what the file already does (line 89).

## Rules that applied and passed

| Rule | Why it passed |
|---|---|
| CHANGE-01/02 | Scope is limited to this change. |
| PR-01, MOD-03 | The new errors and filter follow the existing `relay-denied` error/filter pattern. |
| MOD-02/06 | `FeesService` and `RelayRepository` go through `IChainsRepository`. |
| MOD-05 | No `forwardRef` added. |
| TYPE-01/02 | `z.enum(Const)` matches existing usage, and the schema is in the entity schema file. |
| CONFIG-02 | Config schema, config values and test fixtures were updated together. |
| TEST-01 | Tests use builders, with a fresh builder per case. |
| TEST-08 | Test names were renamed to match their assertions. |
| TEST-05 | The manager is created directly with `new` in the unit spec. |
| License headers | Present on all 25 files. |

All other rules (DB, CACHE, AUTH, SEC, RESILIENCE, DATA, PERF and so on) had nothing in this diff to check.
